lead: Without numbers, in a bad week the owner's impression becomes "it's not working." With numbers, you show what has changed since the baseline. Follow-up is a short, fixed ritual: 20 minutes at the same time, five numbers, one adjustment, and a one-page report. And three signals that call for a visit, not a discount.
objetivo: run the 20-minute check-in, measure 5 indicators against the baseline, and react to the 3 alerts.

aprende.t: Five indicators with the before number
The one-page report, always the same
The 3 alerts and the cadence that tapers off

hero_alt: A short meeting at a small clinic table: three people look at a sheet with a simple bar chart.

secoes.sub: Same time, same agenda, every week. Click each step.

nos.detalhe: The champion's log of questions and the assistant's log (what came in, what went out, what was edited). It's the raw material for the check-in.
Five indicators, always next to the baseline measured before you turned it on. The trend matters more than the number for the week.
5 minutes of numbers, 10 for questions and adjustments made on the spot, 5 to plan the following week. Fixed day and time: "whenever we can" turns into never.
One change at a time to the playbook or the manual, with a new version. Make two changes together and nobody knows which one worked.
Same format every week, sent to the owner even if she doesn't read it at first. Added up, the pages tell the story of the project.

secoes.volta: The following week, the cycle starts again on the same day and time.
secoes.legenda: A short, fixed ritual holds the clinic together better than a long meeting when something breaks.

secoes.sub: Five, not thirty. Collected in a few minutes by the champion, checked by you. No ready-made target: the comparison is with the number from before.

texto: How many messages the assistant prepared or answered. It shows whether it's being used.
On its own it misleads: lots of volume with lots of editing is not a gain.
Time between the patient's message and the first reply, during service hours.
In phase 1 it includes approval time: that's what shows whether the queue is weighing things down.

passos.sub: at the end of the day
texto: Contacts that ended the day with no reply at all. It's the metric from the lesson 1 sheet at Vila Serena (fictional).
It's the number that shows patients lost to delay.
Appointments booked that started in a conversation with the assistant, checked against the schedule.
It shows whether the conversation turns into an appointment, not just a reply.
The champion's estimate of how much reception time was freed up during the week, stated as an estimate.
It's the number the owner feels; that's why it goes with how it was counted written down.

exemplo.texto: Each indicator needs the value from before, measured the same way and in the same kind of week. Without it, the report shows movement, not results. For a deep dive on measuring 30/60/90: Professional 2030 · Consultant, lesson 6.

secoes.sub: Any one of them calls for a visit, a consultant's rule of thumb: in person if possible, within two days, free of charge.

texto: Canceled two check-ins in a row, stopped filling in the log, or doesn't answer messages, even while saying everything is fine.
Often it's overload or an exit in sight: go back to the sheet of roles.
An indicator plunged to near or below the baseline for no reason (holiday, vacation, schedule change).
Usage quietly dropping often comes before quitting.
"I'm deciding whether to continue," "it's weighing on our cash," "I'll check with the team."
When this phrase shows up, the conversation needs to happen face to face, and soon.

exemplo.texto: Listen before defending the system, ask directly "is something bothering you that I'm not seeing?" and leave with a two-week plan. A discount right away doesn't fix the reason.

secoes.sub: Follow-up loosens as the clinic matures. Timeframes are a rule of thumb, adjusted case by case.

texto: In the first weeks, a check-in every week: the clinic is still unsure and the playbook is still changing.
With phase 2 stable and few new questions, every two weeks, with a short message in the week without a meeting.
Stable phase and a confident champion: one conversation a month and a monthly report in place of the weekly one. This is where follow-up turns into maintenance (lesson 7).
New employee, change of service, red alert: back to weekly until things stabilize again.

secoes.sub: Agenda, spreadsheet and report. The tab next to this one shows 4 simulated weeks for Vila Serena, with made-up numbers for the exercise.

secoes.sub: Use the made-up Vila Serena numbers or those of the business you serve.

exercicios.texto: Adapt the 20-minute agenda and fill in the "Before" column of the spreadsheet with the 5 indicators and how to measure each one.
exercicios.pronto: the agenda has the 3 blocks with minutes and a fixed day and time, and the 5 indicators each have a before value, who measures it and how it's measured.

exercicios.texto: Write 4 one-page weekly reports, one for each simulated week. In one of the weeks, include one of the 3 alerts and write the response.
exercicios.pronto: the 4 reports have the same format, the 5 numbers next to the baseline, 1 thing done and 1 next; in the week with an alert, the response is written out (visit, listening, 2-week plan) and no report offers a discount.

secoes.sub: 4 questions. The explanation appears after your attempt.

perguntas.p: Why does each indicator need a before value?
opcoes: Because the assistant's tool doesn't work without a starting value.
Because, without it, the report shows movement and not results.
Because LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) requires recording the business's previous numbers.
Because the owner only accepts numbers she measured herself beforehand.
perguntas.explica: Baseline is the number from before, measured the same way. It's what you compare against to say whether the assistant changed anything.

perguntas.p: The champion canceled the last two check-ins, but says everything is fine. What do you do?
opcoes: Wait one more week, since she said everything is fine.
Send the report by email and stop scheduling meetings.
Offer a discount on the next monthly fee to keep the clinic.
Treat it as a red alert and schedule a visit to listen.
perguntas.explica: A champion who goes quiet is one of the 3 alerts, even with "everything is fine." The response is to go there and listen; a discount doesn't fix the reason.

perguntas.p: In week 3, the contacts with no reply went up from 7 to 8. Is that a red alert?
opcoes: Yes: any rise in any indicator calls for an immediate visit.
Yes, and the assistant should go back to phase 1 immediately.
No, if it has an explanation and does much better than the baseline; it becomes an adjustment at the check-in.
No, because one week's numbers never matter in follow-up.
perguntas.explica: An alert is a sharp drop with no explanation. A small swing with a cause found (the holiday missing from the list) becomes an adjustment to the playbook.

perguntas.p: The clinic has been stable for months and the champion feels confident. What's the cadence?
opcoes: Monthly, with a monthly report in place of the weekly one.
Weekly forever, so the clinic never loses the habit of meeting.
None: the project ended with the handoff.
Daily, to catch any error the same day.
perguntas.explica: The cadence shrinks as things mature: weekly, every two weeks, monthly. If a crisis comes, go back to weekly.

itens.texto: 20 minutes, same day and time: numbers, questions and adjustments, next week.
Always next to the baseline; the trend matters more than the week's number.
Champion goes quiet, a number falling with no explanation, and "I'll think about it": visit and listen, no discount.
Weekly, every two weeks, monthly; in a crisis, back to weekly.
